title: LLM-as-a-Judge for Reliable and Explainable Offline Evaluation in Top-K Recommendation

problem.claim: Offline Top-K recommendation evaluation is intended to guide recommender-system refinement and deployment but may not provide reliable or explainable assessments.

gap.claim: Existing offline evaluation relies on observed user feedback as a preference proxy and produces numerical Top-K scores without meaningful supporting insights.

contributions.claim: The paper identifies reliability and explainability as two fundamental limitations of existing offline Top-K evaluation.

narrative_sequence.summary: Recommendation evaluation guides recommender-system refinement and deployment.
Most existing trials use offline evaluation with Top-K metrics computed over holdout user behaviors.
The paper frames reliability and explainability as two fundamental limitations of this evaluation approach.
Offline evaluation treats observed feedback as a proxy for true preferences and requires rigid ID matching, while incomplete and biased exposure can distort assessments.
Top-K metrics provide numerical scores without meaningful supporting insights, reinforcing the black-box nature of offline evaluation.

source_observation.claim: Observed feedback can be an incomplete and biased proxy for user preferences because item exposure shapes the collected data.

interpretation.claim: Evaluation reliability depends on the relationship between collected feedback, exposure processes, and the preferences being assessed.

application.claim: When designing offline recommendation evaluation, examine exposure bias and proxy validity rather than relying only on rigid ID-matching metrics.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which exposure-bias controls or alternative evaluation procedures are effective.

source_observation.claim: Top-K metrics establish numerical scores without meaningful insights to support them.

interpretation.claim: A scalar evaluation score may be insufficient for understanding why a recommendation system performs as measured.

application.claim: Evaluation workflows should pair performance metrics with explanations that clarify the basis of the assessment.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether explanations improve evaluation decisions or system outcomes.

unknowns: The abstract does not describe the proposed LLM-as-a-Judge method.
No datasets, baselines, experiments, quantitative results, or evaluation protocol details are provided.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported limitations.
